proposal.blind_spot: Store-side write efficiency and which memory unit (L1TEX/L2 vs DRAM) actually saturates first are unmeasured, so DRAM-bound failures with write≈read traffic are indistinguishable from both hard-roofline kernels and on-chip-transaction-bound kernels.

rationale.smsp__sass_average_data_bytes_per_sector: LOW -> write sectors under-filled, DRAM write bytes inflated: restructure stores to full contiguous 128B lines via 128-bit vectorized tl.store and fixed flip/chunk indexing / HIGH -> stores already minimal: cut read traffic instead (fuse multi-pass reads, keep intermediates in registers) or accept roofline
rationale.gpu__compute_memory_throughput.avg.pct_o: HIGH and ~equal to dram__throughput -> DRAM is the roofline: only total-byte reduction helps, leave irreducible streaming kernels unchanged (prevents 0.4x-style regressions) / HIGH and >> dram__throughput -> on-chip L1TEX/L2 unit saturates first: reduce request count with wider vector accesses and register/smem reuse / LOW -> memory headroom exists: raise memory-level parallelism via more loads in flight and block-size retuning

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:A single, balanced split on achieved occupancy (warps_active %) captures the real hardware regime of whether a kernel has enough resident warps to hide latency, whereas candidate 0's 4-way split has a singleton branch (overfit) and candidate 2 adds a redundant metric with an empty quadrant for zero gain over [1].
